tooling.message:
refactor(check): remove the site scope and every site rule from the tooling

## Intent

Every app lives at its developer's hosting, so the rules of lernapps.net's own websites do not belong in the tooling that serves creators; a run on an app hosted elsewhere reported false errors. Readability without JavaScript matters only to lernapps.net's own websites.

## Key changes

- The checks site-check and readable-without-javascript, the page visit without JavaScript and the --site option are gone; --site is now a usage error.
- The rule sections readable-without-javascript and imprint-and-privacy and the scope site leave the skill, the rule-id test, the rule page and the verdict schema; rules that were listing and site are listing only.
- The explainer archetype no longer asks for every page to be readable without JavaScript.
- @lernapps/site becomes a development dependency, used only by the docs site build.
- The architecture no longer names site rules; the glossary explains its changed terms in the prose.

tooling.reason: A follow-up merged as its own pull request (#49) after #47.
tooling.message:
fix(rules): drop the noscript ask from start-page-explains

## Intent

Readability without JavaScript matters only to lernapps.net's own websites, but the interactive archetype's start-page rule still asked apps for a noscript text.

## Key changes

- The rule start-page-explains and its rubric item only ask the start page to say what learners train, for whom and how to begin.

moved.why: Fixes the architecture review warning of the site rule removal (#47).
The follow-up of the site rule removal: no noscript ask for apps.
